study type: Randomized Controlled Trial with longitudinal follow-up
exposure: 8-week pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) program guided by a motion-based intravaginal device
8-week standard home PFMT program following written/video instructions
outcome: Urinary incontinence (UI) symptom improvement (measured by Urogenital Distress Inventory, short-form (UDI-6))
cohort: A total of 363 women with stress or stress-predominant mixed urinary incontinence were randomized into two intervention groups.
finding: Pelvic floor muscle training guided by a motion-based intravaginal device yielded durable and significantly greater urinary incontinence symptom improvement than a standard home program, even in the absence of continued therapy at 24 months.
